engineering-tests-isolate-resourcesengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0 of 0.375 (minor)failPort allocation is dynamic: freePort() listens on port 0 and withPreview passes that port with --strictPort. Termination of every started process is not met. The browser tests (E2E-001, E2E-002 and INT-002) start the preview and Chromium indirectly. Each runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through the shared command() helper (tests/integration.test.mjs:11-20). When that helper times out, it calls child.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) on the npm child alone and rejects at once. It does not await the npm child&#39;s exit, does not signal a process group (spawn has no detached option and there is no negative-pid kill), and does not reach the preview the script started. That preview is spawned at scripts/browser.mjs:34 as a grandchild of npm (package.json:13-14 maps verify and inspect to `node scripts/...`). Its only termination is in withPreview&#39;s finally block (scripts/browser.mjs:54-69), which runs only while the node verify/inspect process keeps executing JavaScript. The complete quoted scripts/browser.mjs and scripts/verify.mjs install no process.on(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) handler and forward no signals. So nothing in the delivered code ties the test&#39;s SIGTERM on the npm wrapper to the preview&#39;s termination. Meanwhile the test rejects and isolated() deletes the working directory (line 33). assertCleanup (lines 43-52) runs only after command() resolves, so it never covers the timeout path. This is the named failure: a test that kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview server running. Panel A (pass) relies on freePort and assertCleanup. Both are accurate, but they cover only runs that finish normally, not the timeout path where the test kills only the wrapper, so they do not settle the requirement. Panel B (pass) itself notes that the timeout path signals only the npm wrapper, then sets it aside as a failure path. The requirement has no exception for failure paths; it requires that every started process be terminated. The material bears out Panel C&#39;s reason, so I rule C&#39;s verdict.tests/integration.test.mjs:16 — the timeout handler runs `child.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;); no(new Error(...))`. The child is the spawned `npm` process (line 13). Its only termination is the finally block at lines 54-69, inside that process. | scripts/browser.mjs:1-100 and scripts/verify.mjs:1-29, quoted in full — neither installs a SIGTERM handler or forwards signals, so nothing in the delivered code makes the test&#39;s SIGTERM on npm re… | tests/integration.test.mjs:43-52 — assertCleanup is called only on resolved results, so the timeout path has no cleanup or assertion. | tests/integration.test.mjs:33 — isolated() removes the temp project once the test rejects, while the descendants it never terminated may still run. | scripts/browser.mjs:11-17 — the port is allocated dynamically, so this clause is met; the fail rests only on termination. | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:11-34 | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:43-52 | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:93-94 | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:137-143 | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:169-176 | quoted lines: package.json:12-14 | quoted lines: scripts/browser.mjs:1-100 | quoted lines: scripts/verify.mjs:1-29 | decider ruling: fail, confirmed by the closed-world span audit | judging basis: decider-fail | tests/integration.test.mjs | package.json | scripts/browser.mjs | scripts/verify.mjs

Each runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through the shared command() helper (tests/integration.test.mjs:11-20). When that helper times out, it calls child.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) on the npm child alone and rejects at once. It does not await the npm child&#39;s exit, does not signal a process group (spawn has no detached option and there is no negative-pid kill), and does not reach the preview the script started. That preview is spawned at scripts/browser.mjs:34 as a grandchild of npm (package.json:13-14 maps verify and inspect to `node scripts/...`). Its only termination is in withPreview&#39;s finally block (scripts/browser.mjs:54-69), which runs only while the node verify/inspect process keeps executing JavaScript. The complete quoted scripts/browser.mjs and scripts/verify.mjs install no process.on(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) handler and forward no signals. So nothing in the delivered code ties the test&#39;s SIGTERM on the npm wrapper to the preview&#39;s termination. Meanwhile the test rejects and isolated() deletes the working directory (line 33). assertCleanup (lines 43-52) runs only after command() resolves, so it never covers the timeout path. This is the named failure: a test that kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview server running. Panel A (pass) relies on freePort and assertCleanup. Both are accurate, but they cover only runs that finish normally, not the timeout path where the test kills only the wrapper, so they do not settle the requirement. Panel B (pass) itself notes that the timeout path signals only the npm wrapper, then sets it aside as a failure path. The requirement has no exception for failure paths; it requires that every started process be terminated. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor accepts that ports are dynamic and that assertCleanup verifies the preview and browser PIDs exited. Their only argument is the timeout branch of command(), which sends SIGTERM to the spawned npm process. That branch runs only if a script hangs for the full 180 s, and nothing in the material shows that happening. In those runs the tests don&#39;t start the preview themselves. The npm script starts it through withPreview as a direct child (process.execPath running vite.js, not an npx wrapper), and that script&#39;s nested finally blocks send SIGTERM and then SIGKILL and wait for the exit. After every run, the tests check through assertCleanup that each logged preview and browser PID is reported as cleaned and no longer exists. INT-003, the one test that starts a preview itself, calls withPreview directly and closes it in finally. The claim that a timeout leaves the server running relies on unshown behavior: the verify script&#39;s signal handling isn&#39;t in the material, and npm normally passes SIGTERM on to the script it runs. So the material doesn&#39;t establish the guidance&#39;s fail case of a test that kills only the wrapper and leaves the preview server running, and the pass stands.","evidence":["scripts/browser.mjs freePort(): server.listen(0, HOST, ...) picks a dynamic port; withPreview passes &#39;--port&#39;, String(port), &#39;--strictPort&#39;","scripts/browser.mjs withPreview: spawn(process.execPath, [resolve(cwd, &#39;node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js&#39;), &#39;preview&#39;, ...]) makes the preview a direct child, not an npx wrapper","scripts/browser.mjs finally: closeBrowser(...), then server.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;), await exited or a 2 s timeout, then server.kill(&#39;SIGKILL&#39;); await exited","tests/integration.test.mjs assertCleanup: assert.match(output, `${kind}: cleaned pid=${pid}`) and assert.throws(()=&gt;process.kill(pid,0)) for every logged preview and browser PID","tests/integration.test.mjs command(): child.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) runs only inside setTimeout(..., timeout), on a hang path the material never shows","tests/integration.test.mjs INT-003 calls withPreview directly with { cwd: dir, viewport }, so the server is the test&#39;s own child and is cleaned up in finally"],"citations":["scripts/browser.mjs","tests/integration.test.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":0,"sample":1}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
